value.description: A vast, slow slug in mottled grey-green skin, ribbed along its pale underside and pitted with a row of dark breathing holes down each flank, its two eye-stalks nodding over a cluster of yellow, finger-like mouthparts. It breathes out a foul, corrosive gas wherever it goes: mostly harmless to the living, but murder on the dead. Anything it passes near rots in minutes into a black, reeking fluid, which the bileworm then happily drinks.

A low, armoured scavenger the colour of old rust, its back a stack of jagged overlapping plates and its eyes two orange beads on short stalks. One enormous saw-toothed claw hangs from its side; it snaps the claw shut on whatever it catches and carries on. It picks across slag and scrap on sharp, dark-tipped legs, and nothing metal or meaty is safe near it.

A heavy, domed beetle in dull slate-black armour, its back one great crown of overlapping plates and its head swept back into a long curved horn. Pale blue light glows in the joints of its limbs and around its jaws, and one oversized hooked forelimb is held ready in front of it. It walks slowly, because nothing it meets has ever made it hurry.
